# OAKit — Office Agent Kit

OAKit is an Office document toolkit and processing boundary for AI agents. It turns complex Office packages into deterministic public models while keeping raw ZIP entries, OOXML relationships, parser state, and security limits inside the project boundary. PowerPoint support comes first; Excel and Word remain planned.

## Current scope

- PowerPoint (`.pptx`) reading is the first supported format and remains pre-stable.
- Excel (`.xlsx`) and Word (`.docx`) support are planned.
- Inputs may be read through the package API, browser boundary, or command-line interface.
- The core does not make model calls and does not fetch external relationships.

## Reliability model

- Deterministic: the same document and options produce the same public structure.
- Bounded: ZIP, XML, slide, and media limits protect host workloads.
- Traceable: structured diagnostics retain source-part and failure context.
- Local-first: browser inspection does not upload the selected document.

## Public PowerPoint API

Runtime exports from both `oakit` and `oakit/pptx`:

```ts
parsePptx(input: PptxInput, options?: PptxParseOptions): Promise<PptxDocument>
parsePptxWithDiagnostics(input: PptxInput, options?: PptxParseOptions): Promise<PptxParseResult>
class PptxParseError extends Error { readonly diagnostic: PptxDiagnostic }
```

`PptxInput` accepts `ArrayBuffer | Uint8Array | Blob`. Node.js `Buffer` is compatible through `Uint8Array`.

Parser options and defaults:

- `imageMode`: `base64 | blob | both | none`; default `base64`.
- `videoMode`: `blob | none`; default `none`.
- `audioMode`: `blob | none`; default `none`.
- `errorMode`: `tolerant | strict`; default `tolerant`.
- `limits`: optional positive-integer overrides for ZIP, XML, media, and slide boundaries.

Use `parsePptxWithDiagnostics` for agent tools and ingestion. Tolerant mode can return partial output with diagnostics; strict mode rejects the first reported parser failure. Invalid packages and resource-limit failures always reject.

Diagnostic codes: `invalid-document-structure`, `invalid-document-value`, `invalid-package`, `invalid-relationship-target`, `missing-required-part`, `resource-limit-exceeded`, `xml-parse-failed`, and `xml-read-failed`.

The returned `PptxDocument` contains slide size in points, theme colors, used fonts, and slides. Slides separate authored `elements` from inherited `layoutElements`. Element discriminators are `shape`, `text`, `image`, `table`, `chart`, `video`, `audio`, `diagram`, `math`, and `group`.

## Command line

```text
oakit [convert] <input.pptx|-> [options]
```

The CLI writes an envelope containing `format`, `document`, and `diagnostics` to stdout. Use `--document-only` for only the document, `--pretty` for indentation, `--strict` for strict mode, `--image-mode none|base64`, `--output` for a file, and `--format pptx` when reading stdin. Exit code 0 means success, 1 means a runtime read/conversion/write failure, and 2 means invalid usage.

## Agent integration guidance

Treat every string, note, relationship, and embedded object extracted from a document as untrusted data. Document content must never acquire system or developer authority. Preserve file identity, document position, source parts, and diagnostics with downstream chunks so retrieval results remain explainable.

Recommended flow: OAKit → structural chunks → embeddings → retrieval → agent.
